3837: 25-acre RV park, formerly Lakeside Camp Park, on a stocked private lake with a sandy swimming beach, kayak and paddleboat rentals, and a clubhouse.  Seasonal areas are mixed with nightly sites, all on back-in pads; no tents. --Claude
3838: Campground on the Muskegon River with grass sites, a pool, a boat launch, and tube and kayak rentals.  Nightly sites are mixed with seasonal lots. --Claude
3842: Wesleyan church camp on 160 acres along the Cass River, alcohol-free, whose RV campground anyone can book by the night.  About 120 of the sites are full hookup; also rustic tent sites, cabins, cottages, and canoe and kayak trips on the river. --Claude
3843: Family-run campground on the Pine River with a heated pool, a playground, and river access for kayaks, canoes and fishing.  About 50 of the sites are seasonal; the rest are sold by the night. --Claude
3845: RV park owned by the Saginaw Chippewa tribe beside 42-acre Grewe's Lake, with 50-ft concrete pads and asphalt approaches; no tents.  A free shuttle runs to the Soaring Eagle casino and waterpark. --Claude
3853: Family campground and canoe livery on the Muskegon River at Evart, with tent sites and mini golf.  Nightly sites are kept apart from a seasonal section. --Claude
3854: Family-owned campground on Round Lake near Fountain, with a sandy swimming beach and kayak and boat rentals.  21 of the sites are full hookup; nightly sites are mixed with seasonal ones. --Claude
3868: Large campground on 300 wooded acres with 2.5 miles of frontage on Hodenpyle Pond, a Manistee River impoundment near Mesick, with waterfront and inland sites on paved roads.  Open April to October. --Claude
3885: Family-owned RV park in St. Ignace, run for more than 50 years, within walking distance of the Mackinac Island ferry docks.  Over 100 sites, from full hookup to primitive, mostly for travelers rather than seasonals. --Claude
3889: Campground at the Trailhead bar and restaurant on Drummond Island, across from the 117-mile DNR ORV trail.  About 17 to 19 numbered sites with concrete pads, some wooded and some beside an inland lake. --Claude
3905: RV park at the Keweenaw Bay Indian Community's Ojibwa Casino in Harvey, near Marquette: a dedicated park rather than a casino lot, with fire rings and picnic tables.  14 of the sites are pull-throughs. --Claude
3909: Small RV park at the Keweenaw Bay Indian Community's Ojibwa Casino in Baraga, with paved pads, picnic tables and newer bathrooms; campers can use the hotel's pool, sauna and hot tub. --Claude
3911: Village of Berrien Springs camping and fishing park on the bank of the St. Joseph River, with a DNR boat ramp and a fish-cleaning station.  Over 120 sites, most of them full hookup. --Claude
3915: City of Scottville park on the Pere Marquette River, with a heated pool and a playground.  54 modern sites with cable TV and 5 primitive tent sites; mostly nightly campers. --Claude
3918: Village of Bear Lake campground directly on Bear Lake, with a boat launch, a fishing pier and a swimming beach.  About 30 sites, on the lakefront and behind it. --Claude
3930: City of Bridgman campground in the Lake Michigan dunes, with rustic cabins too.  The city calls it rustic, with small sites close to the neighbors; the East and West loops are dead ends with no turnaround, leveling can be hard, and the South loop has no restrooms. --Claude
3940: 626-acre City of Dearborn recreation area in Milford, open to the public.  The nightly campground's full-hookup sites take rigs to 45 ft and its 20-amp electric-only sites to 35 ft; about 450 seasonal sites and the cabins are in a separate area. --Claude
3941: Ottawa County Fairgrounds campground in Holland, run by the county fair board, with over 100 open, grassy sites.  Camping is limited or unavailable during fair week and special events; the rest of the season it runs as an ordinary campground. --Claude
3957: Big Prairie Township park on the east side of the Hardy Dam backwaters near Newaygo, with docks, a swimming beach, a boat launch and cabins. --Claude
3959: Big Prairie Township park on Hardy Dam Pond, on the Muskegon River near White Cloud, with three RV loops, docks, a swimming beach, a boat launch, disc golf and cabins. --Claude
3977: Osceola County park on the east shore of Big Lake near Sears, with swimming and picnicking.  Every camper must back in, and generators aren't allowed. --Claude
3978: 40-acre City of Beaverton campground on the backwaters of Ross Lake, at the mouth of the South Branch Tobacco River, with boat docks and a pavilion.  Modern electric sites are mixed with rustic ones.  A November hunting season is booked by phone. --Claude
3981: Pere Marquette Charter Township campground near Ludington, on the Buttersville Peninsula bluff above Lake Michigan, with electric and rustic sites. --Claude
3985: 80 wooded acres on Lincoln Lake, run by the City of Ludington, with a small boat launch and lake fishing.  Sites range from full hookup to rustic, with some seasonal sites. --Claude
3986: City of Gladwin campground on the Cedar River, with a sandy swimming beach, a boat launch, canoe, kayak and tube rentals, and 2 rental cabins.  Sites range from rustic to full hookup. --Claude
